meta.title: How did monthly active users change?
meta.question: How did monthly active users change across the available months?
meta.author: Codex

items: Checks identify the numbered evidence logs, which contain SQL and results.
Unidentified sessions are excluded; session counts are not distinct people.
MAU
Distinct resolved people with a session touching the month.
Resurrected
Active this month, not the prior month, and signed up earlier.

blocks.text: MAU increased every month from 7,937 in April to 11,447 in September: +3,510 (+44.2%). July growth slowed to +162 (+1.6%) before recovering in August (check 3).

items: MAU v1.1: distinct resolved users with a session active span touching the UTC month. Complete months in [2026-04-01, 2026-10-01).
Synthetic dataset; unidentified sessions are excluded (checks 2, 3, 8).
Independent mode; inventory and build checks, Gold trend, Silver recount, identity coverage, growth accounting and acquisition-source partition.
10,400 users signed up before coverage; no pre-April activity is available (check 7).
Monthly gains: +1,197, +842, +162, +733 and +576 (check 3).
June to July: 2,477 new + 2,908 resurrected - 5,223 churned = +162 (check 3).
April to September source changes: paid social +2,436, organic +561, paid search +480, unknown +33 = +3,510 (check 6).
Supported accounting pattern: paid social accounts for 69.4% of net growth. First-touch classification does not establish causality (check 6).
Specific product or marketing causes were not tested.
Gold MAU matches the Silver recount; unidentified sessions comprise 6.5%-7.6% of monthly session records. Their impact on the number of people is unknown (checks 3, 4, 8).
No ambiguous links, mismatches, or activity/profile exceptions found (checks 5, 7).
One session crossed August to September and is included in both; the registry caveat claiming none cross is stale (check 8).
Successful build records reconciliation, but the repository registry hash differs from the build hash. Source fingerprints were not recomputed (check 2).
The coverage interval is documented in the registry, not declared as timestamps in database metadata. The synthetic coverage label is not independent proof.
Pre-coverage activity and causal mechanisms are unknown. Resurrected includes earlier registrants whose first observed activity occurs later.
Monitor monthly MAU with unidentified-session share.
Investigate the July slowdown and paid-social cohort behavior before attributing change to a cause.
